issues.title: Deliver first organization-to-installation slice
issues.body: Local first increment: login, memberships, operator policy, contacts/scope review, manual asset outbox, software and evidence UI/API. Validate tests and docs; track delivered status in docs/validation.md.

issues.title: Validate central NetBox against an isolated live tenant
issues.body: Bundled official NetBox v4.7.3 / netbox-docker 5.1.1 has now been exercised live with tenant-scoped read-only and read/write v2 tokens, devices/VMs/IPs/prefixes, portal writes, upstream write denial and lost-ack recovery. External-mode connectivity to this isolated reference backend is validated too. Remaining: independently deployed instances/versions and legacy authentication, broader site/type/role mappings and operational key policies; no production inventory.

issues.title: Implement complete NetBox source refresh and reconciliation
issues.body: Implemented: devices, VMs, IP addresses and prefixes import atomically after complete scoped pagination; periodic scheduling, queued manual refresh, per-source freshness/errors/counts and source links; missing objects retained with explicit review and reappearance; local software/findings/assessments preserved; source locks serialize import and write-ack recovery. Contract and PostgreSQL concurrency tests plus live bundled integration validate the bounded four-type importer. Strong upstream snapshots, broader topology and monitored production scheduling remain distinct work.

No automatic import or inter-instance synchronization; live compatibility remains tracked separately.

issues.body: Deliver Docker/Python starter with official pinned NetBox, scoped read/write and read-only synthetic tenants, generated credentials and verified TLS, a Bearings worker, repeatable provisioning and preserved volumes. Provide external read-only-by-default configuration without remote writes during bootstrap, private key handling, real functional smoke tests and CI. General inventory import remains separate. Implemented in 06f99a5 with smoke identity guard 3bb32e7. Docker prerequisite diagnostics now explain missing CLI, Compose and engine availability before changing active lab state. Full default startup, live smoke and retained-volume restart passed: https://github.com/rommelfs/bearings/actions/runs/38883987302 . Checks passed 75 tests per database: https://github.com/rommelfs/bearings/actions/runs/38883987223 . External wiring was validated against the pinned reference backend; general inventory import remains separate.

issues.title: Make product monitoring automatic and provide an infrastructure landing overview
issues.body: Implemented local product candidates from exact known names, concrete CPE 2.3 identifiers and supported Log4j package identities; active default enrollment for recognized installed products during software creation, bundled initialization and vulnerability worker. Conflicts require selection; existing mappings, source identity and explicit pauses are preserved. Add a scoped CSRF-protected public vendor/product catalog picker with bounded pagination, source URL isolation, error retention and safe result rendering. The default company/CIRCL landing overview shows action/review/coverage states, current product monitoring, missing versions/inventory/contacts, prioritized assets and concrete next actions/overdue dates with current raw/derived visibility; page auto-refresh is enabled and defers while typing. The original review queue remains at /reviews/. Broader catalog aliases and version-specific patch recommendations remain separate. See docs/user-guide/infrastructure-overview.md. Performance: page-wide grouped counters, eager source loading, bounded per-asset problem windows and batched operator membership checks replace per-company/per-asset queries; query-budget regression covers twelve companies without caching authorization or upstream reads. Runtime verification follow-up: explicit web/worker restarts and health waits in every starter mode, authenticated overview Server-Timing headers and real retained-server/HTTPS browser measurements; local results do not establish user-machine latency. SSO follow-up: timing for real session validation and full inner Django processing, plus a loopback-only verified-TLS web-timing command that uses real existing Keycloak identities, compares HTTP/HTTPS and reports sanitized timing values; user-environment latency remains under investigation. Overview query compilation follow-up: the supplied slow-environment measurements locate the delay inside the view, not SSO/proxy processing. Disable PostgreSQL JIT locally for overview queries and restore the previous setting, including nested transactions/failure rollback. Add numeric per-phase/database/slowest-query timings; stress reproduction and normal real-SSO validation preserve current policy without a shared cache. Priority-query follow-up: post-update measurements still locate a single 6.7–7.3 s SQL call within priorities, so JIT was not confirmed as that environment’s cause. Rank only identifiers before bounded current-policy detail loading, skip legacy lookup for full cards, replace broad legacy/exposure exclusion joins with indexed correlated existence checks, and split ranking/issue/legacy preview timings. Larger synthetic fixtures validate bounded previews and policy behavior; user-machine improvement remains to be confirmed. Further counter/preview refinement after the user confirmed approximately two-second loading: share fresh scoped querysets only within the request, combine related inventory counters, use a correlated latest-risk visibility check, and limit watch/preview field loading. Preserve complete scenario fingerprints and current access checks; seven fewer database executes in paired local comparisons, with a modest company-admin timing gain and a larger CIRCL gain. User-machine improvement remains to be measured.

issues.title: Add email-confirmed private registration and periodic inventory-data reviews
issues.body: Implemented self-registration with minimum IP/range/domain declarations, password set only at email verification, immediate private company-admin workspace and subsequent audited CIRCL-sharing approval. Manual company-reported assets/software never provision NetBox. Configurable owner data-review/repeat intervals, signed snapshot confirmations, persistent deduplicated scheduled service emails, opt-out/current-recipient rechecks and bounded retries. Default local email sink; separately configured TLS SMTP. Infrastructure authority, contact roles and patch verification remain separate. See docs/user-guide/reporting-registration.md. Production mail/bounce acceptance, automated ownership challenges and existing-company invitations remain follow-ups.

Store individual timestamps/text version and show to CIRCL without inventing legacy consent or telephone availability. Remove public schedule/mail switches, ignore forged values, restrict schedule changes to platform superusers or CIRCL with current organization sharing, and enforce required mail in form/service for new-consent registrations. Add emergency telephone to reviewed snapshot fingerprint. DNS TXT/HTTPS, RDAP/provider and reverse-DNS verification remain proposed options, not automatic implementation. See docs/user-guide/reporting-registration.md and infrastructure-verification.md.

issues.title: Explain Bearings benefits with a multilingual static website and shared FAQ
issues.body: Implemented local-only EN/DE/FR/LB static project website focused on free company registration, useful first steps, company/CIRCL use cases and synthetic product screenshots. Nineteen translated FAQs share one content source with docs/faq.md. Five source-reviewed real CVE examples lead with November 2026 NGINX2Root and Java/Java4Shell; humorous personified quotes are explicitly fictional. No customer testimonials, prevention claims, analytics, private-service calls or public hosting. Local registration URL is configurable; a public build rejects localhost registration. Reconciled outdated documentation summaries and added audience-based index, source review and realistic release gates. Real browser/mobile/no-JS/language/FAQ/image checks plus static link/assets validation. Public launch/domain, legal/support details and native-language editorial review remain separate. See website/README.md and docs/product/website-examples.md. Local preview now has a build-before-serve command with an absolute output directory, occupied-port diagnostics and /en/ aliases to avoid missing-build/wrong-directory 404s. Fictional vulnerability testimonial cards are directly reachable from the hero in all languages via #testimonials. Marketing now prioritizes the CIRCL-operated SaaS and free signup; self-hosting promotion, local-start calls to action and technical local-mail details were removed from the public copy. Preview instructions remain developer-only. Continued use of the CIRCL service is explicitly free in all four closing headlines. The unified dev.py website command builds and opens the selected language on HTTP 127.0.0.1, avoiding localhost HSTS upgrades; --no-open supports headless use. No Docker prerequisite or public deployment is needed. The company/CIRCL use-case headline adds a third localized line about the benefit to Luxembourg, preserving both existing audience benefits. Added an owner-requested CIRCL-derived Bearings mark with a connecting ring, the supplied original CIRCL footer logo, and nine locally hosted original project logos with source/checksum provenance, accessible links and responsive layouts. Existing integration maturity wording is preserved; no live connector or public deployment is added. Editorial follow-up: remove template-added outer quote marks that doubled the opening punctuation on Java testimonials. Review all four landing pages, 76 FAQ translations and 20 example quotes/facts/benefits; unify German formal address, improve French/Luxembourgish wording and punctuation, translate remaining screenshot-window/process/CVE-count labels, clarify continued free use and current review-schedule permissions, and update production FAQ with scoped 40000-company test evidence. Real Chromium verified all eight pages at 1440/768/390/360px, exact quote/FAQ text, localized labels, search/empty state, four no-JS FAQ variants, no overflow/JS errors/external requests/cookies. Static local links/assets/fragments pass; no backend behavior or public deployment change.
